Using the new dataset, I want to try and just do cross-validation for the metrics such as log loss, AUC, and balanced accuracy for the main model, since I have already done that for the `ALT2`/`GGT2` models.

# Load Data and Prepare Functions

```{r warning = F, message = F}
# Initial setup
knitr::opts_chunk$set(warning = FALSE, message = FALSE, 
                      fig.align='center', fig.dim=c(10, 8))

# General 
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)

# Modelling and CV
library(nnet)
library(caret)
library(pROC)

# Data
dat.full = readRDS(here("Objects", "dat_full.rds"))

# Helper function for metrics
metrics_summary = function(data, lev = NULL, model = NULL) {
  
  metrics = multiClassSummary(
    data = data,
    lev = lev,
    model = model
  )
  
  c(
    AUC = unname(metrics["AUC"]),
    LogLoss = unname(metrics["logLoss"]),
    BalancedAccuracy = unname(metrics["Mean_Balanced_Accuracy"])
  )
}

# Helper function for getting the final metrics
get_best_metrics = function(model) {
  
  best = model$results[
    model$results$decay == model$bestTune$decay,
    c("AUC", "LogLoss", "BalancedAccuracy"),
    drop = FALSE
  ]
  
  return(best)
}

# Create folds for reuse later
set.seed(2992)
ALT.folds = createFolds(dat.full$ALT3, k = 10, returnTrain = TRUE)
GGT.folds = createFolds(dat.full$GGT3, k = 10, returnTrain = TRUE)

# CV Settings
ALT.cv_control = trainControl(method = "cv", index = ALT.folds,
                          summaryFunction = metrics_summary,
                          classProbs = TRUE)
GGT.cv_control = trainControl(method = "cv", index = GGT.folds,
                          summaryFunction = metrics_summary,
                          classProbs = TRUE)
```

Now, we do the cross-validated fitting, and take metrics.

```{r}
# Fit MLR Models
ALT.mlr.cv = train(ALT3 ~ ExerciseGuidelines + Sex + AlcoholRisk + 
                     SmokingDuration + NonSchoolQuals + IncomeDecile + Age + Waist,
                   data = dat.full, method = "multinom", 
                   trControl = ALT.cv_control, metric = "LogLoss", maximize = FALSE,
                   trace = FALSE)
GGT.mlr.cv = train(GGT3 ~ ExerciseGuidelines + Sex + AlcoholRisk + 
                     SmokingDuration + NonSchoolQuals + IncomeDecile + Age + Waist,
                   data = dat.full, method = "multinom", 
                   trControl = GGT.cv_control, metric = "LogLoss", maximize = FALSE,
                   trace = FALSE)

# Get metrics for later
ALT.mlr.metrics = get_best_metrics(ALT.mlr.cv)
GGT.mlr.metrics = get_best_metrics(GGT.mlr.cv)

mlr.metrics.table = bind_rows(
  ALT = ALT.mlr.metrics,
  GGT = GGT.mlr.metrics,
  .id = "Model"
)

kable(
  mlr.metrics.table,
  digits = 3,
  caption = "Cross-Validated Performance of Multinomial Logistic Regression Models",
  align = "cccc"
)
```

So the models are not particularly much better than the `ALT2`/`GGT2` models. The balanced accuracy still hovers around the $0.5$ mark and AUC and LogLoss are comparable to the logistic regression and GAM models.
